featured.title: US–Iran Conflict Pushes Oil Above $91
featured.content: Renewed fighting between the United States and Iran has sent fresh concerns through global energy markets. Brent crude rose to about $91.05 per barrel while US crude reached about $86.59. Markets remain particularly focused on possible disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for global oil shipments.

articles.title: BREAKING: US–Iran Fighting Pushes Oil Above $91
articles.description: Renewed US–Iran hostilities have increased concerns about global energy supplies. Brent crude rose 0.6% to about $91.05 a barrel while US West Texas Intermediate climbed to about $86.59. Markets are watching the Strait of Hormuz closely because disruption there could affect global oil flows.
articles.imageQuery: Iran US conflict Strait Hormuz oil tanker

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz Remains Central to Global Energy Security
articles.description: The renewed fighting between Washington and Tehran has revived fears of further disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. The strategic waterway previously handled a major share of global oil flows, making any prolonged disruption a concern for fuel prices and inflation.

articles.title: Russian Strikes Hit Kyiv Region for Sixth Straight Day
articles.description: Russian drones and missiles struck Kyiv and surrounding areas as attacks continued for a sixth consecutive day. Reuters reports that four people were killed and more than a dozen injured, including children. Ukrainian officials say diplomatic discussions with US representatives are continuing.

articles.title: Ukraine Peace Efforts Continue Amid Intensifying Attacks
articles.description: Ukraine continues discussions with US representatives over possible peace efforts while Russian attacks against Ukrainian infrastructure remain active. The latest strikes are adding pressure to diplomatic efforts.
articles.imageQuery: Ukraine peace talks Zelensky US representatives

articles.title: Global Markets React to Renewed Middle East Conflict
articles.description: Oil prices, bond yields and global stock markets are reacting to renewed US–Iran military action. Investors are concerned that higher energy costs could increase inflation and put additional pressure on central banks.

articles.title: US–Iran Conflict Creates Fresh Economic Pressure
articles.description: Renewed military action between the United States and Iran is increasing concerns about energy supplies, shipping security and inflation. Markets are closely monitoring developments around the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.imageQuery: US military Iran Middle East conflict

articles.title: Higher Oil Prices Raise Inflation Concerns
articles.description: The renewed jump in crude prices is increasing concerns that energy costs could place additional pressure on inflation and interest-rate expectations in the United States and other major economies.

articles.title: Europe Adds 8.8 GW of New Wind Capacity
articles.description: Europe installed 8.8 gigawatts of new wind-energy capacity during the first half of 2026, nearly one-third more than during the same period last year. Germany was among the major contributors.

articles.title: European Energy Security Remains a Major Priority
articles.description: Higher oil prices and continuing geopolitical tensions are keeping energy security high on Europe's agenda as governments expand renewable generation and seek to reduce exposure to imported fossil fuels.

articles.title: Ukraine Receives Continued European Defence Support
articles.description: European governments continue strengthening support for Ukraine's defence as Russian attacks intensify. The European Union has recently approved additional financial support for defence equipment and related capabilities.
articles.imageQuery: European Ukraine defence support military equipment

articles.title: Nigeria's Economy Grows 4.43% in Q2 2026
articles.description: Nigeria's economy expanded by 4.43% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, up from 3.89% in the previous quarter, according to official data from the National Bureau of Statistics. Growth improved in both the oil and non-oil sectors.

articles.title: Nigeria's Oil Production Also Improves
articles.description: Nigeria's average oil production increased to about 1.72 million barrels per day in the second quarter, compared with about 1.55 million barrels per day in the first quarter.

articles.title: North-Central Nigeria Seeks Stronger Security Cooperation
articles.description: President Bola Tinubu and governors from Nigeria's North-Central region are calling for stronger intelligence sharing and cooperation between governments, communities and security agencies as insecurity continues to affect the region.

articles.title: New Nigerian Armed Forces Pay Structure Takes Effect
articles.description: A previously approved salary increase for members of Nigeria's Armed Forces takes effect from September 1. Reported increases range from 30% to 80% depending on rank, with lower-ranking personnel receiving the largest increases.

articles.title: Nigeria's Economic Growth Faces Security Challenges
articles.description: Nigeria's stronger second-quarter economic performance provides a positive signal, but insecurity, living costs, fiscal pressures and the need to translate economic growth into improved household welfare remain major challenges.

articles.title: Shein Shares Fall 8% in Hong Kong Debut
articles.description: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein saw its shares fall about 8% during its first day of trading in Hong Kong. Investors remain concerned about regulatory pressure, trade risks and the company's changing competitive position.

articles.title: Oil Prices Surge as Middle East Supply Risks Return

articles.title: Yen Remains Near 160 Against the Dollar
articles.description: Japan's yen remains close to 160 per US dollar as investors assess the possibility of another Bank of Japan interest-rate increase. Higher oil prices and US interest-rate expectations are also influencing currency markets.
articles.imageQuery: Japanese yen dollar currency market Tokyo

articles.title: Global Bonds Under Pressure as Oil Rises
articles.description: Global bond markets are facing renewed pressure as higher oil prices increase inflation concerns. Investors are reassessing expectations for interest rates in several major economies.

articles.title: AI Boom Helps Drive Manufacturing Growth Across Asia
articles.description: Demand for AI-related hardware is supporting manufacturing activity across parts of Asia. China, Japan and South Korea recorded manufacturing growth in August, with semiconductor and computer demand contributing to the expansion.

articles.title: Semiconductor Demand Supports Asian Factories
articles.description: Strong demand for chips, servers and other computing equipment linked to artificial intelligence is helping support manufacturing activity across major Asian technology economies.

articles.title: AI Investment Remains a Major Global Economic Story
articles.description: Artificial intelligence continues to drive investment in advanced chips, computing infrastructure and data centres. Markets are increasingly watching whether the investment boom can generate sustainable long-term returns.

articles.title: China–Taiwan Technology and Strategic Rivalry Continues
articles.description: Tensions between Beijing and Taipei continue to affect technology, trade and strategic relations in the Asia-Pacific region as China increases pressure over Taiwan's international participation.

morningSummary.title: MORNING SUMMARY
morningSummary.description: Conflict, energy and economic developments dominate the global picture this morning. Renewed US–Iran fighting has pushed Brent crude above $91 a barrel and revived concerns about disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. Russia has continued strikes around Kyiv while diplomatic discussions remain ongoing. Nigeria's economy expanded 4.43% in the second quarter, showing stronger growth in both oil and non-oil sectors, although insecurity remains a major concern. Across Asia, AI-related demand is supporting manufacturing activity, while China–Taiwan tensions remain significant. Europe is continuing to expand renewable energy capacity as governments seek greater energy security.

bigQuestion: With rising fuel prices, wars and economic pressure affecting countries around the world, can stronger international cooperation prevent today's crises from becoming a bigger global economic problem?
